title: 3 Projects to Become an AI Solutions Engineer
content:
Certificates don't get you hired. PROJECTS do.
If you want to become an AI Solutions Engineer, build these three projects.

First, understand what companies are looking for.
They don't want someone who only knows AI buzzwords.
They want someone who can take a messy business problem and ship a working solution.
And the simplest way to prove that is a portfolio.

Project ONE. An assistant that answers questions from documents.
Upload PDFs, ask questions, and show the source with every answer.
Sources matter.
Businesses don't trust AI answers they can't check.
This one project teaches you retrieval, embeddings and evaluation.
These are the exact skills most AI products are built on today.

But a chatbot alone won't make you stand out.

Project TWO. An agent that completes a real workflow.
Imagine a lead form comes in.
The agent qualifies the lead, adds it to the CRM, and messages the sales team.
Now you are not showing AI. You are showing business value.

Project THREE. Ship that same thing SAFELY.
Add logs, testing, human approval, and a simple dashboard.
Interviews often come back to one question: what happens when the AI is wrong?
If you can answer that, you are ahead of most candidates.

Now the most important part.
Write a public README for every project.
What was the problem? How did you solve it? And where does it still fail?
Writing honest limitations is not a weakness.
It shows maturity.
It tells an interviewer you understand the system, not just the demo.
And clients want the same thing. Honesty.

Then record a short demo video for each project.
Recruiters don't have much time.
A two-minute demo says more than a long resume.
Three projects. Three READMEs. Three videos. That's it.
I'm building in public this month too.
It's one month of work, and it can change your entire profile.
